metric_identity.metric_name: CB Insights State of AI 2025 Report — Comprehensive annual analysis of AI startup funding, deal flow, unicorn formation, M&A activity, and emerging categories across the global AI landscape
metric_identity.source_report: State of AI 2025 Report, CB Insights Research
metric_identity.methodology_notes: Annual full-year report produced by CB Insights using their proprietary predictive intelligence platform. CB Insights tracks 1,500+ tech markets and uses proprietary metrics including Mosaic scores (private company health and growth potential on a 0-1,000 scale) and Commercial Maturity scores. Data derived from CB Insights' venture capital and M&A deal database, which systematically tracks equity funding rounds, exits, and acquisitions globally. The platform aggregates data from SEC filings, regulatory documents, news, and direct submissions. CB Insights also publishes quarterly State of AI reports (Q1, Q2, Q3) throughout the year; this annual report synthesizes the full 2025 calendar year including Q4 data. Supplementary analysis comes from the CB Insights AI 100 list (April 2025) identifying the most promising AI startups.

metric_value.value: Multiple key metrics: (1) Global private AI funding: $225.8B in 2025, nearly double 2024's ~$108B; (2) AI share of total venture funding: 48%, largest on record; (3) OpenAI + Anthropic + xAI combined funding: $86.3B (38% of total AI funding); (4) Q4 2025 funding: $83.2B (OpenAI/Anthropic/xAI captured over half at $46B); (5) Average AI deal size: $49.3M (up 86% from 2024); (6) Mega-rounds ($100M+): 75-79% of total AI funding; (7) 75 new AI unicorns in 2025 (61% of all new unicorns, up from 52% in 2024); (8) LLM developers captured 41% of total AI investment; (9) Robotics captured largest deal share at 11.4% of AI deals; (10) Digital health captured 8.3% of AI deals (down from 12.9% in 2021); (11) Nearly 3 in 4 AI deals still go to early-stage startups; (12) Record AI M&A activity with 172 deals in Q3 alone; (13) Salesforce: most active AI acquirer with 10 acquisitions in 2025; (14) AI 100 list: 27 of 100 companies based outside US, spanning 13 countries; (15) Healthcare (8 companies) and life sciences (6 companies) most represented verticals on AI 100
metric_value.unit: Multiple units: USD billions, percentage, count, multiplier
metric_value.geographic_scope: Global, with specific US focus and international breakdown (AI 100 spans 13 countries including France and South Korea)
metric_value.time_period: Full year 2025 (January-December 2025), with Q4 2025 data extending into early January 2026
metric_value.comparison_baseline: 2024 total AI funding: approximately $108B (2025's $225.8B represents near-doubling); 2024 average deal size: ~$26.5M (2025's $49.3M is 86% increase); 2024 new AI unicorn share: 52% of all new unicorns (2025: 61%); 2021 digital health AI deal share: 12.9% (2025: 8.3%); Q1 2025 funding: $66.6B across 1,134 deals; Q2 2025: $47.3B across 1,403 deals
metric_value.market_layer: cross-cutting (covers model layer through LLM developer funding, infrastructure through compute companies, application layer through vertical AI startups, and cross-cutting through M&A and deal flow analysis)

trend.year_over_year_change: Total AI funding: approximately +109% YoY ($108B to $225.8B); Average deal size: +86% YoY; New AI unicorns as share of all unicorns: +9 percentage points (52% to 61%); AI share of total venture funding: reached record 48%; Mega-round dominance: 75-79% of funding in $100M+ rounds; Robotics maintained deal share at 11.4% while other sectors lost ground; Digital health AI deals declined from 12.9% (2021) to 8.3% (2025); M&A activity hit record levels (172 deals in Q3 2025 alone)
trend.velocity_indicator: time_to_unicorn: 75 new AI unicorns formed in 2025 (61% of all new unicorns), indicating AI companies reach billion-dollar valuations faster than any other tech sector; adoption_doubling_time: Total AI venture funding roughly doubled YoY from ~$108B to $225.8B; Q4 2025 alone ($83.2B) nearly matched all of 2023 funding

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: This is the most granular data source on AI startup funding and deal dynamics. Key signals for entrepreneurs: (1) The extreme funding concentration — three companies (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI) captured 38% of all AI funding at $86.3B — signals that the foundation model layer is not where new startups should compete for capital; the remaining 62% ($139.5B) funds the rest of the ecosystem; (2) 75% of funding flowing through mega-rounds ($100M+) while 3 in 4 deals still go to early-stage companies reveals a barbell market: massive capital pools at the top, many small seed rounds at the bottom, with a potential Series B/C funding gap; (3) The 86% increase in average deal size ($49.3M) suggests investors expect AI startups to be more capital-intensive than previous tech generations; (4) 61% of new unicorns being AI companies confirms this as the dominant venture category for the next cycle; (5) Robotics capturing the largest deal share (11.4%) signals physical-world AI as the next frontier; (6) Record M&A (172 deals in Q3 alone, Salesforce making 10 AI acquisitions) provides viable exit paths beyond IPO; (7) 27 of 100 top AI startups being outside the US, including France and South Korea, validates the global nature of AI opportunity and relevance for European founders.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Founders should not compete with OpenAI/Anthropic/xAI for capital at the model layer — the capital requirements are astronomical ($86.3B combined). Instead, target the application and vertical layers where the majority of deals occur. The 86% increase in average deal sizes means fundraising expectations have shifted — prepare for larger rounds and longer runways. Robotics and physical-world AI represent the fastest-growing deal category; founders in this space have strong tailwinds. The record M&A pace (Salesforce alone made 10 acquisitions) creates viable acquisition exits — design products that large platforms would want to integrate. For European founders: the AI 100 data (27/100 outside US, including France) confirms that non-US AI startups can reach top-tier status.

confidence.cross_reference: Cross-referenced with Stanford HAI AI Index Report 2025 (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report) which reported $109.1B in US private AI investment for 2024 (consistent with CB Insights' ~$108B baseline); State of AI Report 2025 by Nathan Benaich (https://www.stateof.ai/); Lighthouse AI analysis of CB Insights Q3 2025 data (https://lighthouselaunch.com/blog/ai-trends-q3-2025-cb-insights-analysis); Moonfare State of VC 2025 analysis (https://www.moonfare.com/blog/state-of-venture-capital-2025); CB Insights' own quarterly reports Q1-Q3 2025 provide consistent trend lines feeding into the annual figure
confidence.caveats: CB Insights data depends on deal disclosure and may undercount certain regions (particularly China) where funding rounds are not always publicly reported. The $225.8B figure includes equity mega-rounds that can significantly skew averages; excluding the top 3 companies ($86.3B), the remaining ecosystem raised $139.5B. The 48% share of total venture funding partly reflects the concentration of a few massive rounds rather than broad-based AI investment growth. Unicorn valuations are based on last-round pricing and may not reflect secondary market or down-round adjustments. M&A deal counts include acqui-hires and talent acquisitions alongside traditional acquisitions. The annual report was published in early February 2026, capturing some January 2026 deals in its narrative (e.g., xAI's $20B Series E). CB Insights is a commercial research firm and some detailed data requires a paid subscription for full access.
confidence.measurement_reliability: analyst_estimate (CB Insights proprietary deal database aggregating SEC filings, regulatory documents, news sources, and direct submissions; Mosaic scores are proprietary algorithmic assessments; deal sizes based on disclosed funding rounds with some analyst estimation for undisclosed components)
